{{< include _copilot-disclaimer.qmd >}}

This book is a style guide for writing in science, technology,
engineering, and mathematics (STEM).
Most of its examples come from statistics and data analysis,
because statistics and data analysis are the fields that I work in.
Most of its rules apply to any writing that explains technical ideas.

## What the book covers

Most chapters give rules for every kind of technical writing,
such as a paper or a set of lecture notes.
Three chapters cover one kind of document:

- [Paper organization](paper-organization.qmd)
  and [Preparing a manuscript for submission](manuscript-submission.qmd)
  cover research papers.
- [Writing for teaching](teaching.qmd)
  covers lecture notes, slides, and problem sets.

## Who the book is for

I wrote this book for students and mentees
who are learning to write about their research.
I also wrote it for the AI writing assistants
that draft and edit prose for me.

Many rules are stated as checks
that a reader can apply to a single sentence,
so a student and an AI assistant can apply them the same way.
For example,
the section on [demonstrative pronouns](grammar.qmd#demonstrative-pronouns)
asks whether each "this" or "that" is followed by the noun that it refers to.
A person or a program can answer that question
without knowing what the paper is about.

## How the book is organized

The chapters fall into five groups:

- Terms, notation, and evidence:
  - [Defining terms clearly](defining-terms.qmd)
  - [Mathematical notation](notation.qmd)
  - [Citations and evidence](citations-evidence.qmd)
- Papers:
  - [Paper organization](paper-organization.qmd)
  - [Preparing a manuscript for submission](manuscript-submission.qmd)
- Words and sentences:
  - [Word choice](word-choice.qmd)
  - [Avoiding clichés](avoid-cliches.qmd)
  - [Writing for every reader](inclusive-writing.qmd)
  - [Grammar](grammar.qmd)
  - [Conciseness](conciseness.qmd)
- Teaching:
  - [Writing for teaching](teaching.qmd)
- Thinking:
  - [Writing to clarify your thinking](writing-to-think.qmd)

The [Summary](summary.qmd) lists the book's main rules
as a checklist for revising a draft.

## How to read the book

You can read the chapters in any order.
Most sections state one rule and the reason for it,
and then show the rule applied to an example.
Many sections compare a weaker version of a passage with a stronger one.
For example,
the [Word choice](word-choice.qmd) chapter
recommends "before" over "prior to":

> ❌ Prior to fitting the model, we removed outliers.
>
> ✅ We removed outliers before fitting the model.

Definitions, examples, and exercises appear in numbered, colored boxes,
so that other sections and other documents can link to them.

Use the book as a reference while you write,
and use the [Summary](summary.qmd) checklist when you revise.

## Further reading {#sec-further-reading}

These shorter guides cover some of the same ground:

- Novelist Cormac McCarthy's tips on how to write a great science paper [@savage2019]
- Elements of style [@natphys2007elements] - a *Nature Physics* editorial on scientific writing
- The Pathway to Publishing: A Guide to Quantitative Writing in the Health Sciences [@luby2022pathway]
- [Secret, actionable writing tips](https://x.com/acagamic/status/1680381737816424450) -
  a thread on X

For who counts as an author, see the ICMJE criteria in
[Preparing a manuscript for submission](manuscript-submission.qmd).

## Contributing

The book is a work in progress.
If a rule is unclear, wrong, or missing,
open an issue on the book's
[GitHub repository](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/psw/issues).
